nodes.name: IrOx calcination to rutile IrO2
nodes.procedure: IrO2 powder was synthesized by calcining the commercial IrOx (same as that used throughout this work) powder in an alumina boat in a box furnace in air at 450°C for 3 hours. Rutile phase crystallinity was confirmed via PXRD.

nodes.name: Catalyst ink preparation
nodes.procedure: Catalyst ink was prepared by suspending commercial IrOx powder in a mixture of 97% by volume isopropyl alcohol and 3% Nafion 117 solution (Sigma-Aldrich, 5% in a mixture of lower aliphatic alcohols and water). The ratio of catalyst to solution was measured such that drop-casting 12.2 μl of ink onto the GC disk with a geometric area of 0.238 cm² yielded a loading of 80 μg_Ir/cm². Similarly, a separate Vulcan carbon ink was prepared with a ratio of 2 mg_C/ml_ink, with ink liquid volume consisting of 97% isopropyl alcohol and 3% Nafion 117 solution.

nodes.name: GC electrode fabrication
nodes.procedure: The GC disk surface was physically polished on a micro-cloth surface with a 0.05-μm suspended alumina solution, rinsed, and wiped clean. IrOx ink (12.2 μl for 80 μg_Ir/cm² loading) was drop-casted onto the GC disk (0.238 cm² area) and allowed to dry. Vulcan carbon ink (6.1 μl) was then drop-casted on top. The Pt ring was electrochemically cleaned by rapid CV at 200 mV/s from 0.25 to 1.3 V_NHE until stable.

nodes.characterization_summary: Commercial IrOx powder has Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 39.1 m²/g determined from N2 isotherm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The IrOx powder is nanoparticulate (fig. S16) and is relatively high surface area, 39.1 m²/g, as determined from a N2 isotherm and BET surface area analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD pattern of commercial IrOx shows a small amount of Ir metal present.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The powder x-ray diffraction (PXRD) pattern of the commercial IrOx shows that a small amount of Ir metal is present (fig. S17).

nodes.characterization_summary: Rutile phase crystallinity confirmed via PXRD for synthesized IrO2 powder.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Rutile phase crystallinity was confirmed via PXRD.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS used to assess Hg deposition and stripping efficacy on IrOx electrodes; Hg 4f and Ir 5s spectra deconvoluted to identify Hg0 and IrOx species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) is used to qualitatively assess the extent of Hg deposition and efficacy of stripping from the electrode...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show general even dispersion of IrOx on GC disk substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images of electrodes with various IrOx loadings, with and without Vulcan carbon, are provided in the Supplementary Materials (fig. S16). The images show general even dispersion of IrOx on the GC disk substrate.
